title: Void Ending in a Sextile to Jupiter
source: Picatrix (adapted), Book I chapter 5, Book II chapter 3 and Book III chapter 1

<!-- generated by tools/content/gen-void.ts; edit the generator, not this file -->

The sextile is one of the two friendly aspects. Picatrix ties the Moon to the fortunes by trine and sextile whenever a work is meant to prosper, and grades the sextile as the aspect of moderate friendship: the signs it joins are kin in action but not in passion, so the concord between them is a lukewarm one.

When the Moon closes her course in a sign with a sextile to Jupiter, the quiet stretch that follows carries something of his temperate growth. Jupiter is the Great Fortune, hot and humid and temperate, the source of growing power: law, legality, jurisprudence, wisdom, the interpretation of dreams, and the ready winning of requests. His benevolence fits clergymen, kings, and lords; tin is his metal, the emerald and every shining white stone are his, and his animals are the beautiful and harmless ones once used for sacrifice. Set in the ascendant or at mid-heaven, the text says, he rectifies the Moon's misfortunes.
